Anthropic's Claude identifies NIST P-curve seeds came from timestamp-seeded lrand48 PRNG ⭐️ 8.0/10

Anthropic's research shows that the seeds for five major NIST elliptic curves (P-192, P-224, P-256, P-384, P-521) were generated using the C library's lrand48 PRNG seeded with a Unix timestamp, not a cryptographic hash as long speculated. The finding was discovered by Claude in under half an hour and largely debunks decades-old backdoor conspiracy theories, though the B-163 seed remains unexplained.

hackernews · ahlCVA · Oct 16, 18:55 · Discussion

「Why it matters」 This resolves a long-standing cryptographic mystery and significantly weakens 'backdoor' suspicions around widely used NIST curves, providing concrete evidence for developers and security auditors evaluating trust in standardized cryptography.

Tags: #cryptography, #NIST, #elliptic-curves, #AI-research, #security

Mercor: 90% of US working hours fall outside current AI benchmark coverage ⭐️ 7.0/10

Mercor Research mapped O*NET occupational tasks to existing AI benchmark prompts and concluded that 90% of U.S. working hours are spent on tasks with little or no benchmark coverage. The analysis also found that higher-wage occupations are overrepresented in benchmarks even after controlling for AI exposure. The study has not been independently replicated or peer-reviewed, and community commenters note that "covered well" may overstate the adequacy of the few prompts that do exist for many tasks.

hackernews · speckx · Oct 16, 17:08 · Discussion

「Why it matters」 Developers and enterprises lack reliable signals for how models perform on the majority of real-world work, making it difficult to prioritize automation investments or trust vendor claims. The wage-bill bias in benchmarks also means progress on high-value roles may be overstated relative to the broader labor market.

Tags: #AI benchmarks, #labor economics, #O\*NET, #AI evaluation, #workforce impact

Meta's new Business Terms may allow free AI training on news sites ⭐️ 7.0/10

Meta's updated Business Terms, effective October 30, appear to grant the company permission to crawl and scrape websites "associated" with businesses using its platforms — including news publishers — and use that content to develop, improve, research, and train AI, according to a Nieman Lab report cited by The Verge. The terms do not specify compensation for publishers whose content would be used for AI training.

rss · The Verge AI · Oct 16, 14:02

「Why It Matters」 News publishers may lose control over how their content is used for AI training without compensation or consent, potentially undermining existing licensing negotiations and copyright protections. The change affects any publisher using Meta's business platforms, expanding the scope of data Meta can access for AI development beyond its own social platforms.

China drafts tighter AI export controls covering 23 technologies and open-weight models ⭐️ 7.0/10

China's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology released a draft revision to the Catalog of Technologies Prohibited and Restricted from Export on October 16, 2026, proposing to add 40 technologies across AI, biomedicine, and solar PV, with 23 AI-related entries covering foundation models, intelligent agents, computing clusters, and information processing. The draft targets systems above 10^26 FLOPs or 2 trillion parameters, including model weights, source code, and training methods. Public comments are open until November 15, while temporary pre-export registration requirements take effect immediately. Technologies already made public via open-source releases or academic publications are explicitly exempted, and open-sourcing AI technologies qualifies for streamlined automatic licensing. API, app, website, or SaaS access is generally not treated as a technology export, though overseas local deployment of restricted models can fall under the rules. Chinese labs such as DeepSeek and Qwen may face additional compliance steps for future open releases.

rss · The Decoder · Oct 16, 17:42

「Why It Matters」 Developers and enterprises relying on Chinese open-weight models (e.g., DeepSeek, Qwen) should prepare for potential registration or approval delays on new releases that exceed the compute or parameter thresholds, while existing open-source models remain exempt. The fast-track licensing for open-source releases may mitigate disruption, but the immediate pre-export registration requirement adds a compliance layer for any cross-border transfer of model weights or source code not yet publicly released.

Tags: #China, #export controls, #open-weight models, #AI regulation, #geopolitics

Most changes are reviewed and fixed by Claude at least once before human attention is requested, reserving team scrutiny for higher-level questions.

Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours ⭐️ 8.0/10

Google DeepMind announced that four Gemini 4 Argon agents autonomously completed Minecraft from a random spawn in 27 hours and 14 minutes, defeating the Ender Dragon. The agents operated in a sandbox using the Mineflayer library, writing and executing 2,783 programs while coordinating via in-game chat and shared memory without any human-assigned roles or pre-written game logic. The experiment is detailed in a research paper (arXiv:2610.22319) linked from the post.

「Why this matters」 Google DeepMind's first-hand announcement shows four Gemini 4 Argon agents autonomously completing Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours, writing 2,783 programs and coordinating via chat without human intervention. The post links to a detailed technical write-up, making it a concrete, verifiable milestone in multi-agent AI research. With 1.5k likes and 199 replies, it signals strong community interest in autonomous agent collaboration.
